title: Buy gift cards and read out the codes vs. support resolves a gift-card balance query
summary: The recipient recently bought a ShopKart gift card and raised a complaint in the app that its balance did not show up. A caller from "ShopKart support" phones back about that complaint. In the legitimate case, the agent says the glitch is fixed and asks the recipient to add the card in the app themselves and read out only the balance shown. In the fraud case, the caller says the card was "flagged" and that to restore it the recipient must buy a new gift card of the same value and read out its claim code for "verification". Both callers say "gift card", "code", "balance", and "verify".

shared_setting.recipient_profile: the ShopKart customer who raised the complaint; profile sampled at generation.
other_facts: Gift card value: [AMOUNT_25] (₹500–₹10,000), bought by the recipient a few days ago for a relative's birthday.
Both callers quote the complaint reference and the card value.

fraud.label_rationale: The caller tells the recipient to buy a new gift card and read out its claim code. Whoever holds a claim code can spend the value; no legitimate support process needs a customer to buy gift cards or share codes.
fraud.caller_objective: Obtain the claim code of a new card worth [AMOUNT_25], and then more.
stable_facts: The caller says the original card was "flagged for misuse" and will be restored once the account is "verified".
The caller says the new card's value "will be refunded with the old balance".
The caller asks for the full claim code of the new card.

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud caller may ask for more cards of the same kind or split the value; this is the same mechanism. They must not switch to OTPs, card details, links, or app installation. The legitimate agent must not ask for any claim code, OTP, or payment.

must_preserve: gift card, code, balance, and "verify" in both cases
self-entry in app and balance-only check in _L

ambiguities: The word "code" appears in both cases; in _L the recipient uses it themselves and never reads it out.
Knowing the complaint reference and card value is not a cue.
If generation has the fraud caller ask for the code of the original card only, it is still fraud, but that variant is not used here to keep the "buy a new card" action as the evidence.

evidence_references.claim: No legitimate transaction requires payment in gift cards; do not share claim codes; a major marketplace never calls asking customers to buy gift cards (CE12)
A major marketplace states it will never pressure customers to buy gift cards (CE14)
